meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session Feb 8 2024
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 8, 2024 Work Session (with Mayor Pro Tem Mark-Anthony Middleton and Council Member Javiera Caballero excused), the five attending Council members approved excused absences for Caballero and for Chelsea Cook's upcoming February 22 training, approved City Manager Wanda Page's priority items, and read a 46-item docket while pulling supplemental Item 46 (the Israel-Palestine ceasefire resolution) from Consent. During nearly two hours of Item 46 public comment and reflection, Mayor Leonardo Williams described convening a confidential small group of religious leaders and activists and authoring a separate statement alongside Cook's draft resolution. After a recess, Council heard a Water Management presentation on EPA Lead and Copper Rule compliance and voted 5-0 to enter closed session regarding the Darryl Howard and Darryl Dowdy lawsuits.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Excused Absences (Caballero and Cook), and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams convened the work session at 1:00 PM with Nate Baker, Chelsea Cook, DeDreana Freeman, and Carl Rist present, while Mark-Anthony Middleton had a pre-requested excused absence. Council voted 5-0 to excuse Javiera Caballero's absence for the day and 5-0 to excuse Cook's February 22 absence for School of Government training, and heard announcements on Parks and Recreation's 100th anniversary, a Haw Riverkeeper data request, and voting reminders.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items and Reading of Items 1–46
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Wanda Page added Parks and Recreation attachments to citizen matter Item 44 (Chris Hahn) and removed Item 45 (Sarah Maxwell) at the citizen's request; Council approved the priority items 5-0. Mayor Williams read Consent Items 1–38 and public hearing Items 40–43 (Sagebrook annexation, 5802 S. Miami Blvd multifamily annexation, 1339 Cole Mill Rd zoning map change, and remainder lot width text amendment), and Item 46 (ceasefire resolution) was pulled from the consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment and Mayoral Remarks on Israel-Palestine Ceasefire Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Williams managed a large speaker queue for Item 46, with speakers (including Imam Rafiq Zaidi Muhammad, Laura Gibney, and Danielle Mustry in the retained digest portion) urging Council to adopt a ceasefire resolution. Mayor Williams then shared emotional remarks about convening a small confidential group of imams, rabbis, Christian leaders, and activists, noting he had written a statement while Chelsea Cook authored a resolution, before recessing at 3:08 PM.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Moved to Feb 19 General Business Agenda

agenda_items.title: Water Management Lead and Copper Rule Revisions and Setting Feb 19 Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Water Management presented on Durham's 'Lead Safe in Durham' compliance with EPA Lead and Copper Rule revisions, reporting that most corrosion-control test results are below detection levels and introducing an online portal for residents to check or validate service-line materials. City Manager Page then settled the February 19 agenda with Items 1–38 on Consent, Item 46 on General Business, and Items 40–43 as Public Hearings.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Motion on Howard and Dowdy Litigation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Attorney Kim Rehberg read a motion under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) for attorney-client consultation regarding the handling or settlement of Darryl Howard v. City of Durham et al. and Darryl Dowdy et al. v. City of Durham. Council approved the closed session 5-0 by raised hands and recessed to the committee room.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Feb 5 2024
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 5, 2024 regular meeting—Chelsea Cook's first regular session on the dais with Mark-Anthony Middleton on an excused absence—Council approved the consent agenda 6-0 and adopted a Resolution in Support of Black Teens in Crisis (submitted by Wanda Boone) after a friendly amendment from Javiera Caballero. Council members also added a ceasefire resolution/statement to the upcoming Thursday work session agenda and expressed support for Durham Public Schools classified workers, park lead remediation updates, and Walltown small area planning. Following a lengthy public hearing on the Cortez Drive Townhouses zoning map change (Z220040), Council split over housing supply versus Comprehensive Plan Place Type Map compliance, rejecting both the rezoning ordinance and the NCGS 160D-605 consistency statement by hand votes after electronic clickers malfunctioned.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Excused Absence of Mayor Pro Tem Middleton
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams called the meeting to order, DeDreana Freeman led the Pledge of Allegiance, and the Clerk called the roll with six members present (Williams, Nate Baker, Javiera Caballero, Chelsea Cook, Freeman, and Carl Rist). Council formally excused Mayor Pro Tem Mark-Anthony Middleton's absence, which had been requested via email.

agenda_items.title: Council Announcements: Ceasefire Resolution, DPS Workers, Park Lead, and Walltown Planning
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chelsea Cook requested adding a ceasefire resolution and statement to Thursday's work session agenda. Nate Baker voiced support for Durham Public Schools classified workers, requested community updates on unsafe lead levels detected in city parks, supported Walltown/Northgate Mall small area planning added to the JCCPC work program, and backed the inclusive ceasefire resolution, while Mayor Williams recognized Durham School of the Arts.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1-3, 7-14)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Williams read the consent agenda covering board appointments (Environmental Affairs Board, Human Relations Commission, Participatory Budgeting Steering Committee), FY24 CIP closeouts, JP Morgan Chase banking services, service body trucks, Turner & Townsend Heery consulting, HUD grant amendments, the Connect and Protect Behavioral Health grant ordinance, Pace Analytical stormwater lab services, and an amendment with RATP Dev USA for GoDurham fixed-route transit operations. When electronic clickers registered only five of six seated members, Council confirmed approval via hand vote.

agenda_items.title: Resolution in Support of Black Teens in Crisis
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council considered a resolution submitted by resident Wanda Boone supporting Black teens in crisis after prior acronym clarifications. Javiera Caballero moved a friendly amendment to remove paragraph-end Roman numerals and replace the word 'church' with 'faith-based organizations,' which was seconded and adopted unanimously by hand vote.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: Cortez Drive Townhouses (Z220040)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented the Cortez Drive Townhouses rezoning request (RS-20 to PDR 6.003 in Falls/Jordan Lake District B) on roughly 46-47 acres for 282 townhomes, continued from January 16 so the applicant could meet with Chelsea Cook. Residents raised traffic, pedestrian safety, road stub, and buffer-clearing concerns, while council members debated the developer's 3% AMI proffer, $36,000 DPS donation, GoDurham bus pullout, and 1,700 sq ft units against Place Type Map inconsistency and lack of commercial uses; both the rezoning motion and consistency statement failed by hand vote.

votes.item_title: Excuse Absence of Mayor Pro Tem Mark-Anthony Middleton
votes.notes: Mark-Anthony Middleton was excused absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Williams noted that Mayor Pro Tem Mark-Anthony Middleton requested an excused absence via email and entertained a motion to approve it. The motion was moved, seconded, and approved unanimously by voice vote of the six members present.

votes.item_title: Item 5: Resolution in Support of Black Teens in Crisis (as amended)
votes.notes: Mark-Anthony Middleton was excused absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Council considered the resolution submitted by Wanda Boone supporting Black teens in crisis. Javiera Caballero introduced a friendly amendment to remove Roman numerals at the end of paragraphs and replace the word 'church' in the seventh paragraph with 'faith-based organizations,' which was seconded and passed unanimously by hand vote.

votes.item_title: Item 19 (Motion 1): Zoning Map Change Ordinance — Cortez Drive Townhouses (RS-20 to PDR 6.003)
votes.tally: Failed (hand vote; exact count not announced)
votes.notes: Six members were present (Mark-Anthony Middleton excused). Exact numeric tally and individual hand votes of Carl Rist and Chelsea Cook were not read into the record; prior to the vote, Javiera Caballero and Leonardo Williams stated they would support the rezoning while Nate Baker and DeDreana Freeman stated they would oppose it.
votes.discussion_detail: Council voted on Motion 1 to amend the UDO by rezoning the Cortez Drive Townhouses property from Residential Suburban-20 (Falls/Jordan Lake District B) to Planned Development Residential 6.003 (Falls/Jordan Lake District B). Electronic clickers failed to operate, so Mayor Williams conducted a hand vote and declared that the motion failed.

votes.item_title: Item 19 (Motion 2): NCGS 160D-605 Consistency Statement — Cortez Drive Townhouses
votes.tally: Failed (hand vote; exact count not announced)
votes.notes: Mark-Anthony Middleton was excused absent. Hand vote tally and individual hands were not announced on the record.
votes.discussion_detail: Following brief procedural discussion on whether to still vote on the consistency statement after the rezoning ordinance failed, Council moved, seconded, and took a hand vote on Motion 2 to adopt the consistency statement required under NCGS 160D-605, which also failed.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Feb 5 2024
disagreements.issue: Cortez Drive Townhouses Rezoning (Z220040) — Housing Supply vs. Comprehensive Plan Place Type Compliance
disagreements.summary: Council members disagreed over whether to approve a 282-unit townhome rezoning (RS-20 to PDR 6.003) that predated the new Comprehensive Plan and offered affordability and transit proffers, or reject it for lacking commercial uses and deviating from the Place Type Map.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the rezoning because it secures housing supply and developer proffers superior to by-right single-family development.
side_a_arguments: The site already sits inside city limits with water and sewer, allowing 94 single-family homes by right with zero affordability, sidewalk, or bus-stop commitments.

The rezoning secures 3% units income-restricted at 80% AMI for 30 years, 20% smaller 1,700 sq ft townhomes, off-site sidewalk improvements, a $36,000 DPS contribution, and a potential GoDurham bus pullout.
The project began three years earlier prior to adoption of the Comprehensive Plan and delivers townhomes in the $300k range below Durham's average home price.
disagreements.side_b_position: Deny the rezoning because single-use auto-oriented development on a large parcel violates the adopted Comprehensive Plan vision.
side_b_arguments: The 46-47 acre proposal is inconsistent with the Place Type Map's 15-minute mixed-use neighborhood vision and lacks any commercial component.
The Planning Commission recommended denial 8-4, with commissioners warning against classic single-use auto-dependent sprawl in an area with inadequate pedestrian connectivity.
Only 3% of the 282 units are income-restricted and the project entails stream-buffer and environmental impacts without delivering true mixed-use community benefits.
disagreements.resolution: Both the rezoning ordinance and the NCGS 160D-605 consistency statement failed on hand votes.

development_cases.location: East of Angier Avenue (transcribed as Andrew Avenue) between Cortez Drive and Jones Circle (10 parcels, Southeast Durham)
development_cases.scale: Up to 282 for-sale townhouse units on 46.98 acres (10 parcels)
development_cases.zoning_change: RS-20 (Residential Suburban 20) to PDR 6.003 (Planned Development Residential 6.003)

proffers.dps_cash: $36,000 one-time donation to Durham Public Schools
proffers.affordable_housing: Minimum 3% of units (9 of 282) income-restricted at 80% AMI or below for at least 30 years; minimum 20% of units (~56 units) capped under 1,700 sq ft as smaller surface-parked townhomes
proffers.environmental_tree: No new stream crossings beyond existing Cortez right-of-way; tree preservation commitment rather than solely replanting; subject to updated UDO mass grading, phased development, soil/erosion control, and 20% tree coverage at site plan
proffers.transit_infrastructure: All TIA-recommended road improvements; off-site sidewalk along Angier/Andrew Avenue; commitment to build a bus pullout and shelter if accepted by GoDurham at site plan; two vehicular entrances
other_proffers: 100% for-sale townhomes (removed single-family detached homes)

development_cases.tally: Failed (hand vote; exact count not announced)

member_justifications.stance_summary: Caballero supported the rezoning because the site was already in city limits with water/sewer and could be developed by right with 94 single-family homes yielding zero affordable units, no small-unit cap, no off-site sidewalk, no potential bus pullout, and no DPS donation. She argued individual rezonings cannot fix systemic bike/pedestrian or mixed-use policy issues.
member_justifications.key_quote: I will be supporting this because in the context of my choices, 94 single family homes with not 3% affordable housing, not a commitment to a smaller unit... I don't get any of that if it's a by right development.

member_justifications.stance_summary: Baker strongly opposed the 47-acre single-use townhouse project as inconsistent with the Mixed-Use Neighborhood place type in the newly adopted Comprehensive Plan, which envisions walkable 15-minute neighborhoods with commercial and civic uses. Quoting Planning Commissioner Seiz's warning against classic single-use auto-dependent sprawl, Baker stated council must hold the Comprehensive Plan as the floor for rezoning approvals.
member_justifications.key_quote: So for this case, this is a very easy no... this isn't consistent with the vision and the values that we have set forth, that the community has set forth.

member_justifications.stance_summary: Freeman voted no, citing resident concerns over road connectivity and five years of single-use car-dependent sprawl in southeast Durham. She argued that giving up environmental buffers and stream protections across 47 acres requires stronger community benefits than 3% affordable housing and zero commercial space.
member_justifications.key_quote: When we're giving up that much of an environmental impact, it should be something that is of a benefit to the community, and this is not.

member_justifications.stance_summary: Williams supported the project to add missing-middle supply, arguing townhomes priced from the mid-$200s to upper-$300s offer relative affordability compared to Durham's $425,000 average home price. Noting the application began three years prior to the Comprehensive Plan adoption, he urged colleagues not to let 'perfect be the enemy of good' given the 94-home by-right alternative.
member_justifications.key_quote: I don't want perfect to be the enemy of good here... the average housing cost in Durham is 425, and your upper rate is three to high threes, I take that as affordable.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session Jan 18, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: With Mayor Leonardo Williams and Nate Baker excused and Mayor Pro Tem Mark-Anthony Middleton delayed representing Durham during President Biden's visit, senior Council Member DeDreana Freeman presided over the January 18, 2024 work session. Council heard an emergency update on the ongoing power outage and city-county warming shelters, then suspended the rules to pass an FAA Airport Improvement Program grant (Item 6) and a Freese and Nichols Northeast Creek sewer hydraulic model contract (Item 15) 4-0, while referring the Racial Equity Commission appointment back to the Clerk. Council also heard public comment urging a Gaza ceasefire resolution, received major presentations on Participatory Budgeting Cycle 3 winning projects, the Affordable Housing Omnibus, and Bipartisan Infrastructure Law/Inflation Reduction Act grants, and settled the February 5 agenda after Mayor Williams's vote broke a 3-3 tie on the Environmental Affairs Board appointment.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Council Announcements, and Power Outage / Warming Shelter Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presiding Chair DeDreana Freeman opened the work session with Javiera Caballero, Chelsea Cook, and Carl Rist present (Williams and Baker excused; Middleton delayed). Deputy City Manager Bo Ferguson briefed Council on the ongoing electrical outage affecting Durham residents, free GoDurham transit, regional library warming centers, and food and shelter coordination with Durham Congregations in Action and Durham Housing Authority.

agenda_items.title: Suspension of Rules and Action on FAA Grant (Item 6), Sewer Model Contract (Item 15), and Clerk Referral (Item 4)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted 4-0 to accept the Manager's priority items and suspend the rules so time-sensitive grants and contracts could be executed immediately. Council then unanimously approved Item 6 (US DOT/FAA Airport Improvement Program grant 3-37-0056-065-2024 ahead of a Feb 5 deadline) and Item 15 (Freese and Nichols contract for the Northeast Creek sewer basin hydraulic model), and referred Item 4 (Racial Equity Commission appointment) back to the City Clerk.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment on Gaza Ceasefire Resolution, Housing, and Pull of Item 5
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speakers Rachel Salzberg, Elizabeth Rand, Leslie St. Dre, and Stasia Pera urged Council to adopt a permanent Gaza ceasefire resolution drafted by UE150, while George Robeson criticized DHA property maintenance and council governance. Javiera Caballero reported that the Mayor's committee met on MLK Day to draft resolution language, the Clerk clarified four votes are needed to introduce and pass a resolution, and Item 5 (Resolution in Support of Black Teens in Crisis) was pulled to the General Business Agenda for feedback.

agenda_items.title: Board Nominations Update and Setting of February 5 Regular Meeting Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Clerk reported unanimous nominations for Asiah Robertson (Human Relations Commission) and Rosemary James (Participatory Budgeting Steering Committee), and an initial 3-3 tie on the Environmental Affairs Board between Tom Campbell and Artabane. Council voted 4-0 to set the February 5 agenda, and at the close of the meeting (`02:37:40`) the Clerk announced Mayor Williams had cast the seventh vote giving Campbell four votes, allowing Item 1 to return to Consent.

agenda_items.title: Participatory Budgeting (PB) Cycle 3 Update and Winning Projects
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Carmen Ortiz and Fallon Thompson presented the Cycle 3 results, reporting over 12,000 total votes (including 2,886 from DPS students across 16 high schools and 8 middle schools, and over 200 at the Durham County Jail), split roughly evenly between online and paper ballots. They announced five winning projects: DHA security cameras/lighting ($110,000), park lighting ($887,000), sustainable park improvements ($110,000), East Trinity Avenue pedestrian safety ($990,000), and teen rec center equipment (~$85,000).

agenda_items.title: Affordable Housing Omnibus Deep Dive Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayoral interns Bryce McKeel and Joe Wilson synthesized 11 prior housing presentations into five themes: income/affordability, private development constraints, subsidized/public housing under DHA (1,700 units, 5,000+ waitlisted, $50M repair need vs. $15M HUD grant), eviction diversion (most evictions under $1,000; Legal Aid keeping 85 of 120 represented households housed per attorney), and homelessness Continuum of Care gaps. Council members discussed replenishing the exhausted Durham Affordable Housing Loan Fund, reconvening housing stakeholders, and advocating for state-level tenant protections.

agenda_items.title: Bipartisan Infrastructure Law (BIL) and Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) Grants Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City staff updated Council on competitive federal grant pursuits under BIL and IRA, noting a 74% award success rate on submitted applications, recent funding for electric buses, the Village Transit Center, and charging/fueling infrastructure, plus a $500,000 digital inclusion grant application with Central Pines. Environmental Affairs Board speaker Jen Kerrigan and council members stressed clear public communication on grant strategy and staff capacity to manage project delivery.

votes.item_title: Accept City Manager's Priority Items (Items 6, 15, and 18)
votes.notes: Leonardo Williams and Nate Baker were excused absent; Mark-Anthony Middleton was delayed and arrived later in the session.
votes.discussion_detail: Council voted unanimously by raised hands to accept the City Manager's priority additions for Items 6, 15, and 18 onto the work session agenda.

votes.item_title: Suspend Council Rules to Vote on Items 6 and 15 at the Work Session
votes.notes: Four members present during early business.
votes.discussion_detail: To meet the FAA's February 5 execution deadline and expedite flow-monitor installation in the Northeast Creek sewer basin, Council suspended its rules to take final votes during the work session.

votes.item_title: Item 6: US DOT / FAA Federal Airport Improvement Program Grant Offer (3-37-0056-065-2024)
votes.notes: Four members present during early business.
votes.discussion_detail: Under suspended rules, Council unanimously approved the FAA Airport Improvement Program grant offer so the agreement could be returned by the February 5, 2024 federal deadline.

votes.item_title: Item 15: Professional Engineering Services Contract with Freese and Nichols, Inc. (Northeast Creek Sewer Basin Hydraulic Model)
votes.notes: Four members present during early business.
votes.discussion_detail: Under suspended rules, Council approved the engineering services contract with Freese and Nichols, Inc. to install flow monitors promptly and capture both dry- and wet-weather wastewater collection data for hydraulic model calibration.

votes.item_title: Item 4: Refer Racial Equity Commission Appointment Back to City Clerk's Office
votes.notes: Four members present during early business.
votes.discussion_detail: Because the Racial Equity Commission had not yet met ahead of its Saturday retreat, Council approved a request to refer Item 4 back to the City Clerk's office until the next work session.

votes.item_title: Set the Agenda for the February 5, 2024 Regular City Council Meeting
votes.notes: Four members present at 00:46:11; Mark-Anthony Middleton had arrived by the end of the session (`02:39:03`).
votes.discussion_detail: Prior to the afternoon presentations, Council approved the upcoming regular meeting docket placing Items 2, 3, and 7-14 on Consent and Items 1 and 5 on GBA. At 02:37:40, after the Clerk reported Mayor Williams cast the fourth vote for Tom Campbell on Item 1 (Environmental Affairs Board), Item 1 was moved back to Consent without objection.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Jan 16, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Pro Tem Mark-Anthony Middleton while Mayor Leonardo Williams was in Washington, D.C., the January 16, 2024 regular meeting opened with the swearing-in of newly appointed Ward 3 Council Member Chelsea Cook, restoring Council to a full seven-member roster. Council approved Nate Baker's excused absence for the upcoming Thursday work session and unanimously adopted the consent agenda 6-0. In public hearings, Council unanimously adopted both the Teer Quarry UDO text amendment (TC2300003) and companion Eno River District A-2 watershed protection overlay map change (Z230030) to safeguard the new potable water intake, and continued the Cortez Drive Townhouses rezoning (Z220040) to February 5 so the applicant could meet with Council Member Cook.

agenda_items.title: Swearing-In of Ward 3 Council Member Chelsea Cook and Roll Call
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk administered the oath of office to Ward 3 Council Member-Designate Chelsea Cook following her appointment earlier that day, bringing the Council back to seven members. Roll call recorded Middleton, Nate Baker, Javiera Caballero, Cook, DeDreana Freeman, and Carl Rist present, with Mayor Leonardo Williams on an excused absence in Washington, D.C.

agenda_items.title: Human Trafficking Prevention Month Proclamation and Council Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tem Middleton read a proclamation declaring January 2024 Human Trafficking Prevention Month, presented to Kathy Nunes of The Bridge International. Council members welcomed Chelsea Cook, thanked MLK holiday event organizers, and approved Nate Baker's request for an excused absence from the January 18 work session; Middleton noted he would arrive late on January 18 while representing Durham during President Biden's visit, leaving DeDreana Freeman to preside.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1, 2, 4-18)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no items pulled, Council unanimously adopted the consent agenda covering minutes, Environmental Affairs Board appointment, an Open Table Ministries emergency shelter contract, rear-mount ladder fire trucks, and major roadway, pavement preservation, sidewalk repair, traffic signal, and transit engineering contracts (Items 6-18).

agenda_items.title: Text Amendment: Teer Quarry (TC2300003)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff (Aaron Cain) presented UDO text revisions to Articles 4, 8, and 12 establishing watershed protection standards for the new Teer Quarry potable water supply intake, allowing existing lots of record to follow prior rules until redevelopment. Following a public hearing with no speakers, Council unanimously approved both the ordinance amendment and the NCGS 160D-605 consistency statement.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: Teer Quarry Watershed Overlay (Z230030)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: As the companion map change to Item 20, staff presented the reclassification of parcels within a half-mile of the Teer Quarry intake from Eno River Districts A and B into the Eno River District A-2 watershed protection overlay required by the NC Environmental Management Commission (already adopted by Durham County on Jan 8). Council asked about well/boring protections and unanimously approved the map change and consistency statement 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: Cortez Drive Townhouses (Z220040)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff noted the Planning Commission recommended denial 8-4 in June 2023 and reported two new applicant proffers: at least 3% of units income-restricted at 80% AMI or below for 30 years and a $36,000 one-time donation to Durham Public Schools. The applicant's representative requested a continuance to February 5, 2024 to meet with newly seated Council Member Chelsea Cook, and Council kept the public hearing open to that date.

votes.item_title: Approve Excused Absence for Council Member Nate Baker (Jan 18, 2024 Work Session)
votes.notes: Mayor Leonardo Williams was on an excused absence in Washington, D.C.
votes.discussion_detail: Nate Baker requested an excused absence for the Thursday, January 18 work session. DeDreana Freeman moved and Javiera Caballero seconded approval, passing 6-0 (the Clerk initially misread 7-0 and corrected the tally to 6-0).

votes.item_title: Item 20 (Motion 1): Text Amendment Ordinance — Teer Quarry (TC2300003)
votes.notes: Mayor Leonardo Williams was excused absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Council adopted the UDO text amendment revising Articles 4 (Zoning Districts), 8 (Environmental Protection), and 12 (Infrastructure) to establish watershed rules for the Teer Quarry water intake.

votes.item_title: Item 20 (Motion 2): NCGS 160D-605 Consistency Statement — Teer Quarry Text Amendment (TC2300003)
votes.notes: Mayor Leonardo Williams was excused absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the required NCGS 160D-605 consistency statement for the Teer Quarry UDO text amendment.

votes.item_title: Item 21 (Motion 1): Zoning Map Change Ordinance — Teer Quarry Watershed Overlay (Z230030)
votes.notes: Mayor Leonardo Williams was excused absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Council adopted the zoning map amendment removing affected parcels within a half-mile of the Teer Quarry intake from Eno River Districts A and B and establishing the Eno River District A-2 watershed protection overlay.

votes.item_title: Item 21 (Motion 2): NCGS 160D-605 Consistency Statement — Teer Quarry Watershed Overlay (Z230030)
votes.notes: Mayor Leonardo Williams was excused absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the NCGS 160D-605 consistency statement for the Teer Quarry Watershed Overlay zoning map change.

meetings.title: Special Durham City Council Meeting - Ward 3 Vacancy Jan 16 2024
meetings.executive_summary: At a 9:30 AM special meeting to fill the Ward 3 seat vacated when Leonardo Williams became mayor on December 4, 2023, the six seated council members initially deadlocked 3-3 between Sheila Huggins (backed by Williams, Mark-Anthony Middleton, and Nate Baker) and Chelsea Cook (backed by Carl Rist, Javiera Caballero, and DeDreana Freeman). After debate over whether to use ranked-choice voting or allow a special election, Baker shifted his vote to Cook as a compromise to achieve the required four-vote majority. Following a 4-2 hand vote confirming Cook, Middleton noted the 4-2 count for the record before changing his vote to Cook as an act of goodwill, and Mayor Williams declared the selection unanimous.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Ward 3 Selection Procedure
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams called the special meeting to order with all six seated members present (Williams, Mark-Anthony Middleton, Nate Baker, Javiera Caballero, DeDreana Freeman, and Carl Rist). He outlined that four votes were required to appoint a successor from the four finalists (Amanda Borer, Chelsea Cook, Sheila Huggins, and Chastin Swain), or else the vacancy would proceed to a special election.

agenda_items.title: Deliberation, Compromise, and Appointment of Chelsea Cook to Ward 3 Seat
agenda_items.discussion_summary: In first-round statements, Williams, Baker, and Middleton backed Sheila Huggins while Rist, Caballero, and Freeman backed Chelsea Cook, creating a 3-3 deadlock. After Freeman, Rist, and Baker expressed support for ranked-choice voting while Middleton opposed it and declined to name a second choice, Baker compromised to switch his vote to Cook, producing a 4-2 hand vote that Middleton subsequently joined as an act of goodwill so Cook's appointment was recorded unanimously.

votes.item_title: Appointment of Chelsea Cook to Fill the Vacant Ward 3 City Council Seat
votes.notes: Initially 3-3 (Huggins vs. Cook), then 4-2 for Cook on the hand vote (Middleton and Williams not voting for Cook initially), then changed to unanimous 6-0 at 00:26:08.
votes.discussion_detail: After an initial 3-3 split between Sheila Huggins (Williams, Middleton, Baker) and Chelsea Cook (Rist, Caballero, Freeman), Nate Baker compromised and shifted his vote to Cook to reach the four-vote threshold. A hand vote confirmed Cook 4-2 (Baker, Caballero, Freeman, Rist in favor), after which Middleton raised a point of order noting the 4-2 tally and changed his vote to Cook as an act of goodwill, and Mayor Williams declared the final vote unanimous for Cook.

disagreements.meeting_title: Special Durham City Council Meeting - Ward 3 Vacancy Jan 16 2024
disagreements.issue: Ward 3 Vacancy Candidate Selection and Ranked-Choice Voting vs. Special Election
disagreements.summary: Council deadlocked 3-3 between Legal Aid housing attorney Chelsea Cook and attorney/community leader Sheila Huggins, sparking a procedural debate over whether to break the tie via ranked-choice voting or trigger a special election.
disagreements.side_a_position: Appoint Chelsea Cook (and support ranked-choice voting to resolve council deadlocks rather than defaulting to a special election).
side_a_arguments: Chelsea Cook brings deep expertise in affordable housing, eviction defense, and tenants' rights from Legal Aid that complements the dais.

DeDreana Freeman, Carl Rist, and Nate Baker argued ranked-choice voting offers a constructive compromise mechanism to select a broadly acceptable candidate when no one reaches four first-choice votes.
disagreements.side_b_position: Appoint Sheila Huggins as 'day-one ready,' and reject ranked-choice voting as an improper effort to avoid an election.
side_b_arguments: Sheila Huggins demonstrated mastery of city departments and prior council decisions during interviews and had previously earned thousands of Durham votes.

Mark-Anthony Middleton stated he had no second choice and argued Council's charter duty is to make a good-faith effort, not to use ranked-choice voting to avoid returning the seat to voters in a special election.
disagreements.resolution: Nate Baker shifted his vote from Huggins to Cook to reach a 4-2 majority; Mark-Anthony Middleton then changed his vote to Cook as an act of goodwill and Mayor Williams declared the appointment unanimous.

meetings.title: Special Durham City Council: Ward 3 Vacancy Jan 10, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: The January 10, 2024 special City Council meeting was a dedicated public comment session allowing supporters to speak on behalf of the four finalists for the vacant Ward 3 council seat. With all six seated council members present and each finalist allocated up to 30 minutes of combined virtual and in-person testimony, supporters spoke in turn for Chastin Swain, Sheila Huggins, Chelsea Cook, and Amanda Borer. No deliberations or formal votes were taken, and Mayor Williams announced Council would reconvene at 9:30 AM on Tuesday, January 16 to cast its final selection vote, with the appointee to be sworn in that evening.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Candidate Support Hearing Format
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams called the candidate support meeting to order, the Clerk called the roll with all six seated members present, and Williams reminded attendees that Council would strictly listen while supporters spoke for up to 30 minutes per finalist across online and in-person speakers.

agenda_items.title: Public Support Comments for Chastin Swain
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Online and in-person supporters of Chastin Swain highlighted his collaborative leadership, governance and policy experience, humility, and commitment to climate and sustainability goals. Following the final speaker, Mayor Williams thanked attendees and transitioned to the next candidate's allotted block.

agenda_items.title: Public Support Comments for Sheila Huggins
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Supporters of Sheila Huggins emphasized her Ward 3 residency, legal background, long-standing community service, knowledge of city departments and budget processes, empathy, and ability to listen to residents across Durham.

agenda_items.title: Public Support Comments for Chelsea Cook
agenda_items.discussion_summary: In-person and remote speakers supporting Chelsea Cook—including legal colleagues, educators, and longtime friends—praised her eviction-defense work at Legal Aid, deep commitment to Durham's vulnerable residents, understanding of local history and equity, and ability to build consensus across differing viewpoints.

agenda_items.title: Public Support Comments for Amanda Borer and Next-Steps Announcement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Supporters of Amanda Borer—including local business owners and aging/caregiving advocates—highlighted her coalition-building work for older adults and direct care workers, incisive questioning, and dedication to preserving Durham's character. Mayor Williams announced Council would vote on Tuesday, January 16 at 9:30 AM and swear in the appointee at 7:00 PM that evening before adjourning at 9:09 PM.

meetings.title: Special City Council Meeting: Ward 3 Vacancy Jan 8, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: On January 8, 2024, the six seated members of the Durham City Council held a special meeting to conduct public interviews of the four finalists for the vacant Ward 3 seat: Amanda Borer, Chelsea Cook, Sheila Huggins, and Chastin Swain. After answering candidate questions regarding the 30-minute supporter-comment rules for the January 10 meeting, each council member engaged each finalist in a five-minute Q&A covering land use, SCAD and gentrification, affordable housing, economic development, public safety, and budget priorities. No votes were taken, and Council reiterated the schedule for the January 10 supporter session and January 16 selection and swearing-in.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Procedural Clarifications for Jan 10 Support Hearing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams called the meeting to order with all six seated members present and noted the City Manager and City Attorney were seated in the gallery while Council ran the interview session directly. Williams answered candidate questions confirming each finalist had 30 total minutes for virtual or in-person supporter remarks on January 10, with virtual speaker info due to the Clerk by 1:00 PM Wednesday.

agenda_items.title: Ward 3 Finalist Interview: Amanda Borer
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Amanda Borer introduced her work on two local nonprofit boards serving older adults and caregivers and fielded five-minute Q&A rotations from council members. She discussed addressing gentrification and SCAD impacts in historically Black neighborhoods, workforce development for direct care workers, gun violence prevention, higher-density walkable housing, and reducing reliance on cars.

agenda_items.title: Ward 3 Finalist Interview: Chelsea Cook
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chelsea Cook highlighted her legal and community experience working directly with Durham residents facing housing, food, and healthcare trade-offs across DHA, DSS, and NIS systems. Council members questioned her on equity versus equality, housing stability, and how she approaches disagreements while ensuring marginalized voices have a seat at the table.

agenda_items.title: Ward 3 Finalist Interview: Sheila Huggins
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Sheila Huggins completed a two-minute introduction and five-minute dialogue rotations with each council member. Council members probed her views on prior council land-use and policy decisions, city operations, racial equity, and navigating policy disagreements.

agenda_items.title: Ward 3 Finalist Interview: Chastin Swain and Procedural Closing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chastin Swain discussed his legal and state government service (DHHS, OSBM, DNCR), tax and city-staffing considerations, using the UDO rewrite to manage displacement and preserve community culture, affordable housing, and public safety balancing community investment with policing. Council closed by reviewing the January 10 supporter-speech rules and January 16 selection and swearing-in schedule before adjourning at 9:34 PM.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session Jan 4, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 4, 2024 work session, Council members discussed pursuing federal BIL/IRA climate funds and diverged on whether small area planning (including Walltown/Northgate Mall) should start at the Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC) or in a Council work session. The City Attorney received informal concurrence to support an NC Supreme Court amicus brief on COVID-19 restaurant business-interruption insurance, while residents delivered over an hour of sharply divided public comment on a proposed Gaza ceasefire resolution. Council also reviewed the Equal Business Opportunity Program (EBOP) update and disparity study plans, heard the Clerk announce four Ward 3 finalists (Amanda Borer, Sheila Huggins, Chelsea Cook, and Chastin Swain), unanimously set the January 16 agenda 6-0, and voted 6-0 to enter closed session under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3).

agenda_items.title: Roll Call and Council Announcements on Federal Climate Grants and Small Area Planning
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With all six seated members present, Carl Rist urged timely staff reporting on federal BIL and IRA climate grant opportunities, which staff agreed to bring to an upcoming work session. Nate Baker proposed bringing a broad small area planning resolution (including Walltown and Northgate Mall) to a work session, prompting debate with Javiera Caballero and Mark-Anthony Middleton over whether land-use work program items should originate at JCCPC.

agenda_items.title: NC Supreme Court Amicus Brief Request (COVID-19 Business Interruption Insurance)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant City Attorney Anne-Marie Tosco briefed Council on a request for Durham to join an amicus brief before the North Carolina Supreme Court supporting 16 local restaurants seeking COVID-19 business-interruption insurance coverage, continuing the previous council's Court of Appeals brief. Council members gave informal concurrence to proceed.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Matter on Gaza Ceasefire Resolution and Pulled Consent Items (Items 3, 7, 12)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Yilta Kahana urged Council to focus on local anti-Semitism and property damage rather than international affairs, while numerous in-person and virtual speakers (including Leslie St. Dre, Raina Risenko, and Emily Wilkes) urged Council to pass UE150's permanent Gaza ceasefire resolution; Javiera Caballero and Mayor Williams outlined the convening committee and resolution-drafting process. Council also deferred Item 3 (Black Teens in Crisis resolution) to the next work session for edits and heard pulled comments on street repaving/sidewalks (Items 7 and 12) from Nate Baker and resident David Bradway.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Item 3 deferred to next work session

agenda_items.title: Finance Presentation: Equal Business Opportunity Program (EBOP) Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy CFO Sheila Faucette presented the history, staffing, and priorities of the Underutilized Business Compliance (UBC) division administering EBOP and SLBE programs, noting plans for an updated ordinance rewrite, improved vendor data collection, HUB certification outreach, and a budget request for a new disparity study. Council members questioned MWBE goal-setting performance, inclusion of disability-owned businesses, multilingual technical assistance, and direct local developer support.

agenda_items.title: Ward 3 Vacancy Schedule, Set Agenda for Jan 16, and Finalist Announcement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed the Ward 3 interview and supporter-hearing schedule and voted unanimously 6-0 to set the January 16 regular meeting agenda (Consent: Items 1, 2, 4-18; GBA public hearings: Items 20-22). Following a brief break for tally synchronization, the Clerk announced the four Ward 3 finalists receiving four or more nominations: Amanda Borer (4), Sheila Huggins (5), Chelsea Cook (4), and Chastin Swain (4).

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Pursuant to NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Attorney Kimberly Rehberg read the statutory motion to enter closed session for attorney-client consultation regarding a settlement demand for a yet-to-be-filed liability claim. Council approved the motion 6-0 by hand vote.

votes.item_title: Set the Agenda for the January 16, 2024 Regular City Council Meeting
votes.notes: All six seated members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Council voted unanimously by hand vote to settle the January 16 regular meeting agenda with Consent Items 1, 2, and 4-18 and General Business public hearings Items 20-22.

votes.item_title: Enter Closed Session Pursuant to NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3) (Attorney-Client Consultation)
votes.notes: All six seated members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Following the reading of the motion by City Attorney Kimberly Rehberg, Council voted 6-0 by hand vote to convene in closed session under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with counsel concerning a settlement demand for a yet-to-be-filed liability claim.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Work Session Jan 4, 2024
disagreements.issue: Procedural Pathway for Small Area Planning (Council Work Session Resolution vs. JCCPC Referral)
disagreements.summary: Council members differed over whether to initiate a small area planning discussion—including Walltown and Northgate Mall—directly on a City Council work session agenda or route it first through the Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC).
disagreements.side_a_position: Bring the small area planning discussion or resolution to a City Council work session so all council members can provide input early.
side_a_arguments: Nate Baker noted rules of procedure were unclear and wanted a work session discussion on small area planning beyond just Northgate Mall within a feasible staff timeline.
Carl Rist noted he was no longer on JCCPC and wanted an opportunity for his voice to be heard at a full Council work session.
disagreements.side_b_position: Originate land-use work program items at the JCCPC because planning jurisdiction is shared with the County.
side_b_arguments: Javiera Caballero noted land-use issues fall under both City Council and County Commissioners and recommended placing the item on the February JCCPC agenda first.
Mark-Anthony Middleton added that resolutions are aspirational rather than binding staff directives and noted any JCCPC work product still returns to full Council for debate.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken; members aired preferences ahead of staff work-program scheduling.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Jan 2, 2024
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 2, 2024 regular meeting—the first session of the new year with all six seated members present—Council proclaimed January 2024 National Mentoring Month, adopted the consent agenda 6-0 (excluding Item 7), and voted 5-1 to approve a Racial Equity Commission appointment over DeDreana Freeman's objection requesting re-advertisement. Following continuances of two rezoning cases (Items 21 and 22) to February 19, Council split 2-4 to reject the East Club Gateway voluntary annexation and utility extension agreement with Gander Development LLC (Item 23), with Baker, Caballero, Freeman, and Rist voting no over Comprehensive Plan Transit Opportunity Area compliance and unprohibited multifamily uses. Council then unanimously passed an Omnibus 18 Planning Department mailed-notice fee ordinance 6-0, approved pulled Item 7 ($240,000 CDBG contract with Families Moving Forward) 6-0, and excused Mayor Williams's upcoming January 18 absence 6-0.

agenda_items.title: National Mentoring Month Proclamation and Council Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams read a proclamation designating January 2024 as National Mentoring Month and presented it to Mr. Langley. During council announcements, Mark-Anthony Middleton addressed recent shootings and reported online harassment of residents speaking from affected neighborhoods.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1, 3-6, 8-18, 25-27)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously approved the consent agenda 6-0 (excluding pulled Item 7), encompassing the Mayor's Council for Women appointment, homelessness and rapid rehousing contracts (Project Access, Housing for New Hope, Urban Ministries), elevator and Durham Arts Council agreements, Byrne Justice Assistance Grant ordinance, stormwater and biosolids contracts, HDR PFAS consulting, and the Northeast Creek sewer interlocal agreement with Durham County.

agenda_items.title: Racial Equity Commission Appointment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DeDreana Freeman requested re-advertising the Racial Equity Commission seat to seek candidates with professional racial equity experience. Mark-Anthony Middleton objected that Council had already reached consensus at the work session and should not disparage the volunteer applicant publicly; the appointment passed 5-1 with Freeman voting no.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Continuances: Sagebrook (Z220019) and 5202 South Miami Blvd Multifamily (Z220061)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff reviewed Item 21 (Sagebrook, Z220019/BDG220013, referred from October 2023) and Item 22 (5202 South Miami Blvd Multifamily, Z220061/BDG230008, working through phased grading and tree preservation rules). At the applicants' requests and with staff concurrence, Council kept both public hearings open and continued both items to February 19, 2024.

agenda_items.title: East Club Gateway Annexation, Utility Extension & Zoning (Z220062 / BDG220031)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and Katie Hamilton of Gander Development presented a 13.96-acre contiguous annexation and Commercial General (CG) textual development plan at East Club Boulevard and I-85, noting a 7-5 Planning Commission recommendation. Javiera Caballero and Nate Baker criticized the omission of August Planning Commission comments from the packet, the failure to prohibit multifamily housing in CG, and weak design standards inconsistent with Transit Opportunity Area goals, while Middleton praised the local firm's nuisance prohibitions and $15,000 housing proffer; Motion 1 failed 2-4.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Planning Department Notice Fee Ordinance Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant Planning Director Grace Smith presented an ordinance updating mailed public notice fees to cover expanded notification distances from 600 feet to 1,000 feet under Omnibus 18 (effective January 1, 2024), including correcting an unadjusted $104 fee to $460. Following a public hearing with no speakers, Council approved the fee ordinance 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Families Moving Forward CDBG Contract (Item 7) and Excused Absence for Mayor Williams
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After discussing resident input on pulled Item 7, Council unanimously approved 6-0 a three-year $240,000 CDBG contract with Families Moving Forward for emergency shelter case management and supportive services. Council then voted 6-0 to excuse Mayor Williams's January 18 work session absence to attend the U.S. Conference of Mayors.

votes.item_title: Item 2: Racial Equity Commission Appointment (Mr. Williams)
votes.notes: DeDreana Freeman voted no.
votes.discussion_detail: After DeDreana Freeman asked to re-advertise the vacancy for candidates with professional racial equity experience and Mark-Anthony Middleton objected that consensus had already been reached at the work session, Mayor Williams called the vote and the appointment passed 5-1.

votes.item_title: Item 23 (Motion 1): East Club Gateway Voluntary Annexation and Utility Extension Agreement (Gander Development LLC, BDG220031)
votes.notes: Clerk announced 'four to two with Baker, Caballero, Freeman and Rist voting no.'
votes.discussion_detail: Council voted on Motion 1 to adopt an annexation ordinance effective March 31, 2024 for the 13.96-acre East Club Gateway site and authorize a utility extension agreement with Gander Development LLC. The motion failed 2-4 with Baker, Caballero, Freeman, and Rist voting no, rendering subsequent zoning and consistency motions unnecessary.

votes.item_title: Planning Department Fee Ordinance Update (Omnibus 18 Mailed Public Notice Expansion)
votes.notes: All six seated members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Following a public hearing with no speakers, Council unanimously adopted the ordinance updating Planning Department mailed-notice fees to reflect the Omnibus 18 expansion from 600 feet to 1,000 feet.

votes.item_title: Item 7: Contract with Families Moving Forward ($240,000 CDBG Supportive Services and Emergency Shelter)
votes.notes: All six seated members present.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Jan 2, 2024
disagreements.issue: Racial Equity Commission Appointment vs. Re-Advertisement for Professional Experience (Item 2)
disagreements.summary: DeDreana Freeman sought to re-advertise a Racial Equity Commission vacancy to recruit candidates with professional racial equity experience, while Mark-Anthony Middleton opposed revisiting a consensus work-session selection.
disagreements.side_a_position: Re-advertise the appointment to recruit applicants with professional racial equity expertise.
side_a_arguments: As an advisory body to Council, the Racial Equity Commission would benefit from members possessing professional experience in racial equity.
disagreements.side_b_position: Proceed with the scheduled vote on the volunteer applicant already selected by work-session consensus.
side_b_arguments: The proper time to request re-advertisement was during the work session rather than at the regular meeting after the applicant's name became public.
Pulling or rejecting the nomination at this stage risks sending an unfair message that the volunteer resident is deficient or unfit.
disagreements.resolution: Council proceeded to a formal vote and approved the appointment 5-1, with DeDreana Freeman voting no.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Jan 2, 2024
disagreements.issue: East Club Gateway Voluntary Annexation and General Commercial Zoning (Z220062 / BDG220031)
disagreements.summary: Council split 2-4 over whether to annex 13.96 acres at East Club Boulevard and I-85 for a Commercial General textual development plan, weighing Transit Opportunity Area design standards and Comprehensive Plan fidelity against applying current UDO rules for a local developer.
disagreements.side_a_position: Deny the annexation and rezoning because the textual development plan falls short of Comprehensive Plan Transit Opportunity Area standards and leaves multifamily housing unprohibited.
side_a_arguments: Under Commercial General zoning without a housing prohibition, up to 90 residential units could still be built without addressing site constraints.
The proposal lacks strong urban design commitments beyond a partial build-to zone and could result in an auto-oriented strip center with a sea of parking inconsistent with the TOA place type.
Missing August Planning Commission comments and the need to uphold the newly adopted Comprehensive Plan ahead of the UDO rewrite warranted a no vote.
disagreements.side_b_position: Approve the annexation and rezoning as consistent with current UDO rules and the future Place Type Map.
side_b_arguments: The site is designated Transit Opportunity Area on the future place type map, and the applicant cannot use downtown design districts in the suburban tier until the UDO is rewritten.
Gander Development is a small, two-year-old local firm that offered an extensive list of prohibited nuisance uses, a perimeter fence, and a $15,000 affordable housing contribution.
Council should apply existing rules consistently rather than making anticipatory rulings against smaller local developers.
disagreements.resolution: Motion 1 for voluntary annexation and the utility extension agreement failed 2-4, ending consideration of the rezoning.

development_cases.development_type: Commercial / Mixed-Use (Commercial General with Textual Development Plan)
development_cases.scale: 13.96 acres across 7 parcels (up to 90 residential units max due to NCDOT access limits, though no residential planned initially)

proffers.transit_infrastructure: Remove existing I-85 exit ramp driveway; consolidate access to one driveway on East Club Boulevard with two 6-foot sidewalks; build-to zone west of Duke Energy transmission line
other_proffers: Minimum of 3 distinct uses required on site

Prohibited nuisance uses including group living, hospitals, cemeteries/mausoleums/columbaria/memorial gardens, electronic gaming, firing ranges, nightclubs/bars, paintball, payday lenders, veterinary clinics/kennels, and vehicle sales/leasing/rentals/service
6-foot privacy fence along eastern property line prior to start of construction

member_justifications.stance_summary: Caballero questioned why residential uses remained allowed on a prime Transit Opportunity Area parcel without stronger design standards. She warned that without binding design commitments, the CG(D) zoning could result in a strip mall with excessive surface parking, concluding the applicant had not met her burden for approval.
member_justifications.key_quote: What I don't want is a strip mall with a lot of parking... that burden hasn't been met for the standard that I need to get to yes.

member_justifications.stance_summary: Baker echoed Caballero's concerns and noted he had voted against the case on the Planning Commission because it fails to advance the Comprehensive Plan's Transit Opportunity Area goals for walkable, people-oriented design. He argued the partial build-to zone and absence of design commitments could still produce a sea of parking, and urged council to enforce the new Comprehensive Plan and pursue targeted UDO updates.
member_justifications.key_quote: I also don't see the requested zoning being consistent with the comprehensive plan... we have a brand new comprehensive plan, we've got a place type map, it's not consistent with the place type map, so in my view, we should use the plan.

member_justifications.stance_summary: Middleton supported the rezoning and annexation, praising the local Durham-based developer for an exhaustive list of prohibited uses and noting the staff report found it consistent with the future place type map. Because the UDO rewrite was not yet complete, he argued council should evaluate applications under existing rules rather than anticipatory standards.
member_justifications.key_quote: The UDO has not been rewritten, and I've said time and time again I want to be consistent in making decisions that are based upon what the rules are right now as opposed to kind of anticipatory rulings.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session Dec. 19 2023
meetings.executive_summary: The December 19, 2023 Work Session opened with council members urging residents to call 911 upon hearing gunfire and approving three procedural motions adding priority items from the City Manager and City Clerk and setting the January regular meeting agenda. During Citizen Matters, residents raised allegations of Public Works permitting delays on Ardmore Drive—to which Deputy City Attorney Don O'Toole responded regarding an unsupported slope—alongside extensive public comment urging a Gaza ceasefire resolution, a $25/hour city worker wage floor, and full funding for the HEART program. Council also received the final report and recommendations from the Community Safety and Wellness Task Force, including a proposed three-year pilot Office of Survivor Care, and finalized the Ward 3 vacancy questionnaire timeline ahead of a December 21 deadline.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Council Comments, and Addition of Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams called the work session to order at 1:00 PM with five members present and Carl Rist arriving later. Mark-Anthony Middleton urged residents to call 911 whenever they hear gunfire, City Manager Wanda Page added supplemental Items 26 (CentralSquare Technologies) and 27 (Mid-Atlantic Associates), the City Attorney sought thumbs-up consensus on an amicus brief defending DACA, and Council added the Clerk's Ward 3 vacancy questionnaire discussion to the end of the agenda.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed Unanimously (hand votes on priority additions)

agenda_items.title: Ardmore Drive Permitting Dispute, Gaza Ceasefire Resolution, and City Worker Wages
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Eno River Association Executive Director Jessica Sheffield presented the 2024 wall calendar, and resident Isaac Woods alleged retaliatory Public Works delays on his new construction at 905 Ardmore Drive, prompting Deputy City Attorney Don O'Toole to cite an unsupported vertical cut slope and water ponding requiring engineering certification. Numerous speakers then urged Council to adopt the UE150 permanent Gaza ceasefire resolution, raise city worker pay to $25/hour, and expand 24/7 HEART funding.

agenda_items.title: Racial Equity Commission Appointment and Training Requirements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DeDreana Freeman pulled Item 2 to relay feedback from commission members that newly appointed members lacked baseline racial equity training. Mark-Anthony Middleton recalled that completing racial equity training was originally part of the task force commitment, and Mayor Williams agreed to coordinate with Equity and Inclusion Director Sharon Williams.

agenda_items.title: Grant Project Resolution for Bell Street Stormwater Improvements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DeDreana Freeman requested a construction timeline for the Bell Street stormwater project. Public Works project manager Antoine Williams stated that design is scheduled to finish in August 2024, bidding is targeted for January 2025, and construction is expected to conclude in late 2026.

agenda_items.title: Community Safety and Wellness Task Force Final Report and Recommendations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community Safety Director Ryan Smith introduced task force co-chairs Xavier Cason and Marcia Owen, Prescriptions for Repair coordinator Asmen Johnson, and Reverend Allen Jones, who reviewed two and a half years of work and five core recommendations including Naloxone distribution, trauma healing, and funding a three-year Office of Survivor Care pilot. Carl Rist and Javiera Caballero endorsed the Office of Survivor Care, while Mark-Anthony Middleton and Mayor Williams urged pairing survivor care with concrete upstream prevention investments.

agenda_items.title: Ward 3 Vacancy Questionnaire and Special Election Timeline
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk announced nominations for Alicia Sutton (Mayor's Council for Women, Ward 2) and David G. Williams (Racial Equity Commission, At-Large), and Council finalized the Ward 3 vacancy questionnaire for release December 21 through January 3 with three initial applicants already filed. Javiera Caballero reported Board of Elections guidance that if Council deadlocks and requires a special election, it could not appear on the March primary ballot and would likely fall in November 2024.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Agenda for Next Regular City Council Meeting and Ceasefire Discussion Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Wanda Page presented the docket placing Items 1, 3-19, 26, and 27 on Consent, Item 2 on General Business, and Items 21-24 on GBA Public Hearings, which Council approved. Before adjourning at 3:13 PM, Mayor Leonardo Williams asked Council to set aside a dedicated four-hour session to craft a council-authored response on the Middle East conflict rather than adopting an external resolution.

votes.item_title: Add City Clerk Priority Item (Ward 3 Vacancy Questionnaire Discussion) to Agenda
votes.notes: Carl Rist was noted as on the way at the 00:02:43 roll call and joined the meeting later.
votes.discussion_detail: The City Clerk requested adding discussion of the Ward 3 vacancy questionnaire to the end of the work session agenda so it could be finalized and posted on Thursday, December 21. Council moved, seconded, and approved the addition by unanimous hand vote prior to Carl Rist's arrival.

votes.item_title: Add City Manager Priority Items 26 and 27 (CentralSquare Technologies & Mid-Atlantic Associates) to Agenda
votes.notes: Hand vote taken before Carl Rist arrived.
votes.discussion_detail: City Manager Wanda Page requested adding supplemental Item 26 (CentralSquare Technologies LLC services agreement for Emergency Communications) and Item 27 (Mid-Atlantic Associates Inc. contract amendment) to the agenda. Council moved, seconded, and approved adding both items by unanimous hand vote.

votes.item_title: Set the Agenda for Next Regular City Council Meeting (Consent: 1, 3-19, 26-27; GBA: 2; Public Hearings: 21-24)
votes.notes: All six seated members were present by this vote.
votes.discussion_detail: City Manager Wanda Page read the settled docket for the upcoming regular City Council meeting, shifting Item 2 (Racial Equity Commission appointment) to the General Business Agenda at DeDreana Freeman's request while keeping Items 1, 3-19, 26, and 27 on Consent and Items 21-24 as GBA public hearings. Council approved the settled agenda by unanimous hand vote.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Work Session Dec. 19 2023
disagreements.issue: City Response to Calls for a Permanent Gaza Ceasefire Resolution
disagreements.summary: Following extensive public comments urging Durham to adopt UE150's permanent ceasefire resolution and redirect funds toward local wages and HEART, Mayor Leonardo Williams declined to adopt an externally authored resolution and noted Council lacked consensus on a single approach, proposing a dedicated four-hour council working session instead.
disagreements.side_a_position: Decline externally authored resolutions and convene a four-hour council session to draft an inclusive, council-authored statement or resolution.
side_a_arguments: Durham's municipal budget has no line item funding foreign wars.
Signing onto an externally authored resolution without council deliberation risks community division and broader repercussions.
Individual council members hold differing views, requiring structured space to reach a holistic response.
disagreements.side_b_position: Public speakers and community advocates demanded immediate introduction and passage of the UE150 ceasefire resolution.
side_b_arguments: Over 19,000 Palestinians have been killed and municipal resolutions apply political pressure on federal officials.
Durham has precedent taking international human rights stances such as opposing South African apartheid.
Taxpayer funds should be prioritized for $25/hour city worker wages and 24/7 HEART funding.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken; Council members voiced no objection to Mayor Williams's request to schedule a dedicated four-hour working session to craft a council response.
