meetings.title: Durham City Council Dec. 18, 2023
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 18, 2023 regular City Council meeting, Council rejected a three-month, $52,356 contract extension for the ShotSpotter gunshot-detection pilot by a 2-4 vote, leaving the system to go dark while the Wilson Center completes its independent evaluation. Council approved the Consent Agenda (6-0), the Page Road/Greenwood annexation and 70-townhome rezoning (4-2, with a doubled $35,000 affordable housing proffer), the Rose of Sharon Road 46-townhome rezoning (6-0), UDO Omnibus 18 (6-0), Pedestrian Mall UDO text amendment (6-0), and Conservation Subdivisions UDO text amendment (5-1, DeDreana Freeman opposed). Council also held the FY24-25 HUD Annual Action Plan public needs hearing and passed pulled Items 5 (FY24-25 budget schedule) and 6 ($350,000 ARPA grant to Be Connected Durham) unanimously (6-0).

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Items 1-4, 7-10, 12-16 Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams read the consent agenda, noting that Items 5 (FY24-25 budget schedule) and 6 (Be Connected Durham ARPA project) were pulled for separate consideration and Item 11 (ShotSpotter) was on the General Business Agenda. Council approved the remaining consent items including the FY23 ACFR, ARPA affordable housing interlocal agreement, Legal Aid eviction diversion amendment, and GoDurham electric buses.

agenda_items.title: ShotSpotter / SoundThinking Contract Amendment (3-Month Pilot Extension)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Fifteen in-person and three virtual speakers addressed the $52,356 three-month extension of the ShotSpotter contract, with critics citing false positives, lack of proven violence reduction, and uncompleted Wilson Center evaluation, alongside pleas for a Gaza ceasefire and youth investments. Javiera Caballero, Carl Rist, Nate Baker, and DeDreana Freeman opposed extending the contract prior to receiving the Wilson Center report, while Mark-Anthony Middleton and Mayor Leonardo Williams argued for continuity until March.

agenda_items.title: FY 2024-2025 Annual Action Plan Public Needs Hearing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community Development Director Reginald Johnson opened the first of two required HUD public needs hearings for approximately $2.0M in CDBG, $1.3M in HOME, $150K in ESG, and $1.06M in HOPWA funds. High school senior Seth Hurley and housing advocate Stella Adams urged focusing funds on public housing, preserving naturally occurring affordable housing, and serving households at or below 30% AMI, including city workers.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation & Rezoning: Page Road / Greenwood (70 Townhouses)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented Greenwood Homes' request to annex roughly 10 acres in the 2900 block of Page Road and rezone it from Rural Residential to PDR 7.827 for up to 70 townhouses. The applicant doubled its dedicated housing fund proffer from $17,500 to $35,000 prior to first certificate of occupancy, and Council approved the annexation and rezoning 4-2 with Nate Baker and DeDreana Freeman voting no, followed by a 6-0 consistency statement.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: 3317 and 3325 Rose of Sharon Road (46 Townhouses)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pam Porter of TMTLA Associates and Toledo Builders presented a 7.5-acre rezoning from RS-20 to PDR 6.400 for up to 46 townhouses, increasing proffers to $16,000 for Durham Public Schools, $29,000 for the dedicated housing fund, a 12-foot multi-use path, and curb ramps. Council praised the local family-owned builder and unanimously approved the rezoning and consistency statement.

agenda_items.title: UDO Text Amendment: Omnibus 18
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented Omnibus 18, expanding rezoning mail notice radii from 600 to 1,000 feet, adding multi-family tenant signposting, replacing special use permits with rezoning for DPS schools, allowing two driveways for duplexes, removing infill tree-coverage exemptions, and prohibiting creating nonconformities. After Stella Adams asked about childcare facility impacts and staff confirmed the updates aim to expand childcare opportunities, Council approved both motions 6-0.

agenda_items.title: UDO Text Amendment: Pedestrian Mall Maximum Width
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff and applicant Jeremy Anderson of Thomas & Hutton presented an amendment increasing maximum pedestrian mall width from 50 feet to 75 feet, or up to 100 feet when additional amenities such as public art, landscaping, or outdoor seating are provided. Council approved the amendment and consistency statement 6-0.

agenda_items.title: UDO Text Amendment: Conservation Subdivisions (Article 6)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Assistant County Attorney Curtis Massey and Planning Director Sara Young presented an expedited amendment clarifying that conservation subdivisions must meet objective standards in UDO §6.2.4.H rather than all 12 general purpose statements in §6.2.4.A, following pending appellate litigation against the county. Opponents urged waiting for the Court of Appeals ruling, while Mayor Pro Tem Middleton argued for preemptive legal clarity and Nate Baker called for broader rural planning reforms; the ordinance passed 5-1 with DeDreana Freeman dissenting.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item: FY 2024-2025 Budget Development Schedule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Stella Adams pulled Item 5 to argue that submitting council budget priorities in January leaves the public little influence before the March 18 public hearing, urging increased affordable housing funding and permanent city worker raises. Mayor Williams noted a pay study is underway, and Council adopted the budget schedule 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item: ARPA Subrecipient Grant Agreement with Be Connected Durham
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Williams noted Item 6 had been pulled mistakenly without contention. Council unanimously authorized the City Manager to execute an ARPA subrecipient grant agreement with Be Connected Durham and Beyond for the Fayetteville Street Corridor Equitable Engagement Series in an amount not to exceed $350,000.

votes.item_title: Approve Consent Agenda (Items 1-4, 7-10, 12-16; excluding Pulled Items 5, 6, and GBA Item 11)
votes.notes: Items 5 and 6 were pulled for separate discussion at the end of the meeting.
votes.discussion_detail: Council approved all non-pulled consent agenda items—including the FY23 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report, ARPA affordable housing interlocal agreement with Durham County, TG Allen UDO engagement contract, Legal Aid eviction diversion amendment, and GoDurham electric bus purchase—by unanimous 6-0 electronic vote.

votes.item_title: Item 11: Authorize 3-Month Contract Amendment with SoundThinking Inc. for ShotSpotter Services ($52,356; Total $249,856)
votes.notes: Clerk announced motion failed 4-2 (i.e., 2 in favor, 4 opposed) with Baker, Caballero, Freeman, and Rist voting no.
votes.discussion_detail: Following extensive public comment overwhelmingly opposing ShotSpotter and council debate over waiting for the Wilson Center's independent evaluation of the 12-month pilot, the motion to extend the contract through March 14, 2024 failed 2-4, causing the ShotSpotter alert service to go dark.

votes.item_title: Item 17 (Motion 1): Adopt Annexation Ordinance and Utility Extension Agreement for Page Road / Greenwood
votes.notes: DeDreana Freeman cited the lack of affordable housing units on site in voting no.
votes.discussion_detail: Council voted 4-2 to annex two parcels at the 2900 block of Page Road effective December 31, 2023 and authorize a utility extension agreement with Greenwood Homes Raleigh LLC for up to 70 townhouses, with the applicant increasing its dedicated housing fund proffer to $35,000.

votes.item_title: Item 17 (Motion 2): Adopt UDO Zoning Map Amendment for Page Road / Greenwood (RR to PDR 7.827)
votes.discussion_detail: Council approved the zoning map change from Residential Rural (County) to Planned Development Residential 7.827 (City) for up to 70 townhome units by a 4-2 vote.

votes.item_title: Item 17 (Motion 3): Adopt NCGS 160D-605 Consistency Statement for Page Road / Greenwood
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the statutory consistency statement associated with the Page Road / Greenwood zoning map change.

votes.item_title: Item 18 (Motion 1): Adopt UDO Zoning Map Amendment for 3317 and 3325 Rose of Sharon Road (RS-20 to PDR 6.400)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved rezoning 7.5 acres at 3317 and 3325 Rose of Sharon Road to PDR 6.400 for up to 46 townhouses by Toledo Builders, incorporating proffers of $16,000 for DPS, $29,000 for the dedicated housing fund, a 12-foot multi-use path, and curb ramps.

votes.item_title: Item 18 (Motion 2): Adopt NCGS 160D-605 Consistency Statement for Rose of Sharon Road
votes.discussion_detail: Moved by DeDreana Freeman and seconded by Carl Rist, Council unanimously adopted the consistency statement for the Rose of Sharon Road rezoning.

votes.item_title: Item 19 (Motion 1): Adopt UDO Text Amendment Omnibus 18
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved Omnibus 18 revisions across UDO Articles 3, 5, 6, 7, 9, 14, and 17, matching the Board of County Commissioners' 4-0 approval on December 11.

votes.item_title: Item 19 (Motion 2): Adopt NCGS 160D-605 Consistency Statement for UDO Omnibus 18
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the statutory consistency statement for UDO Omnibus 18.

votes.item_title: Item 20 (Motion 1): Adopt UDO Text Amendment for Pedestrian Mall Maximum Width (Article 16)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved amending UDO Article 16 Section 4 to allow pedestrian malls up to 75 feet wide, or 100 feet wide with qualifying public amenities.

votes.item_title: Item 20 (Motion 2): Adopt NCGS 160D-605 Consistency Statement for Pedestrian Mall Amendment
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the consistency statement for the Pedestrian Mall UDO text amendment.

votes.item_title: Item 21 (Motion 1): Adopt UDO Text Amendment for Conservation Subdivisions (Article 6)
votes.discussion_detail: Council approved amending UDO Article 6 (§6.2.4) to clarify that conservation subdivisions are governed by the objective standards in §6.2.4.H rather than all 12 general purposes in §6.2.4.A, passing 5-1 with DeDreana Freeman voting no.

votes.item_title: Item 21 (Motion 2): Adopt NCGS 160D-605 Consistency Statement for Conservation Subdivisions
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the consistency statement for the Conservation Subdivisions UDO text amendment.

votes.item_title: Item 5: Adopt FY 2024-2025 Budget Development Schedule
votes.discussion_detail: Following citizen comments from Stella Adams requesting greater public input prior to council budget priority setting, Council unanimously adopted the FY 2024-2025 budget development schedule.

votes.item_title: Item 6: Authorize ARPA Subrecipient Grant Agreement with Be Connected Durham and Beyond (Not to Exceed $350,000)
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously authorized the City Manager to execute a $350,000 ARPA subrecipient grant agreement with Be Connected Durham and Beyond for the Fayetteville Street Corridor Equitable Engagement Series.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Dec. 18, 2023
disagreements.issue: Three-Month Contract Extension for ShotSpotter / SoundThinking Pilot
disagreements.summary: Council split 2-4 over whether to pay SoundThinking $52,356 to keep ShotSpotter active for three months while the Wilson Center completes its independent evaluation of the 12-month pilot.
disagreements.side_a_position: Let the pilot contract expire as scheduled and await the Wilson Center evaluation before making any further commitment.
side_a_arguments: Extending the contract for three months yields no new evaluation data because the Wilson Center study only covers the completed 12-month pilot.
Community speakers cited false positives, missed shootings, and lack of proven crime reduction.
Resources should prioritize preventative community investments and evidence-based evaluation.
disagreements.side_b_position: Approve the $52,356 three-month extension to maintain continuity of gunfire detection until the Wilson Center report arrives in March.
side_b_arguments: Funds were already available within the Police Department budget and cutting service mid-review leaves shooting victims without alerts when 911 is not called.
Families and residents in high-gunfire areas reported valuing faster police response and recovered shell casings.
Keeping sensors active avoids operational disruption if Council decides to continue after reviewing the report.
disagreements.resolution: Motion failed 2-4, terminating the ShotSpotter alert service upon expiration of the 12-month contract pending the Wilson Center report.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Dec. 18, 2023
disagreements.issue: Page Road / Greenwood Annexation and 70-Townhome Rezoning Without On-Site Affordable Units
disagreements.summary: While four members approved the Page Road / Greenwood annexation and rezoning after the developer doubled its housing fund proffer to $35,000, two members voted no due to the absence of on-site affordable units.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve annexation and PDR 7.827 rezoning for up to 70 townhouses with an increased $35,000 dedicated housing fund proffer.
side_a_arguments: The project adds needed townhome housing supply contiguous to city services and aligns with the mixed residential neighborhood place type.
The developer doubled its dedicated housing fund contribution from $17,500 to $35,000.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose the rezoning and annexation because the development lacks on-site affordable units.
side_b_arguments: New townhome developments in Durham should include actual affordable units rather than relying solely on modest cash proffers.
A no vote signals to other developers that stronger affordability commitments are expected.
disagreements.resolution: Both the annexation/UEA and zoning map amendment passed 4-2, and the consistency statement passed 6-0.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Dec. 18, 2023
disagreements.issue: Conservation Subdivisions UDO Text Amendment Amid Pending Appellate Litigation
disagreements.summary: Council debated whether to adopt an expedited UDO amendment clarifying that conservation subdivisions need only meet §6.2.4.H objective standards rather than all 12 general purposes in §6.2.4.A while a lawsuit against Durham County is before the Court of Appeals.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt the clarifying text amendment immediately to align the UDO with 15 years of planning practice and insulate the City from litigation.
side_a_arguments: Reading §6.2.4.A's 12 aspirational purposes as mandatory makes conservation subdivisions legally impossible to approve.
Objective, measurable criteria in §6.2.4.H protect primary conservation areas without exposing the City to lawsuits.
Stronger environmental protections in Falls Lake and Southeast Durham were addressed through phased grading and belong in the UDO rewrite.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose the amendment over environmental enforcement concerns in Southeast Durham and dissatisfaction with removing purpose-statement safeguards.
side_b_arguments: Existing conservation subdivisions in Southeast Durham have caused severe sediment runoff into waterways.
Modifying the purpose-statement language before the Court of Appeals rules does not adequately strengthen environmental protection.
disagreements.resolution: The UDO text amendment passed 5-1 (DeDreana Freeman opposed), and the consistency statement passed 6-0.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session Dec. 7, 2023
meetings.executive_summary: In his first work session as Mayor on December 7, 2023, Leonardo Williams led Council through pulled consent items, the FY23 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report audit, and establishing the Ward 3 City Council vacancy appointment process. Council debated the three-month $52,356 ShotSpotter contract extension (Item 11)—which Javiera Caballero pulled to the General Business Agenda—while reviewing ARPA funding for Be Connected Durham (Item 6) and Durham County joint affordable housing projects (Item 7). External auditors Cherry Bekaert reported clean unmodified opinions for FY23 with one significant deficiency in year-end accounts payable cutoff, and Council unanimously adopted a 60-day City Charter appointment timeline targeting a Ward 3 vote on January 16, 2024.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Council Remarks, and Manager Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Williams called the 1:00 PM work session to order with all six seated members present and noted his selection to the Harvard-Bloomberg New Mayors Academy. City Manager Wanda Page added a 20-minute ACFR presentation for Item 4 and noted zero-lot-line language was removed from Item 19 (UDO Omnibus 18), which Council approved by hand vote.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Remarks on Youth Workforce, Charter Education, and Gaza Ceasefire
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deworn Langley of the Charles Hamilton Houston Foundation requested city investment in career pathways for boys and young men of color; Lukeshia Alston presented her Prepertory Academy Charter High School and research initiatives; and Brad Young urged Council to avoid one-sided foreign policy resolutions and focus on extremism on both sides if addressing a ceasefire.

agenda_items.title: ARPA Project: Be Connected Durham Fayetteville Street Corridor Equitable Engagement Series
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DeDreana Freeman questioned why Be Connected Durham's $500,000 request was funded at $350,000. Deputy City Manager Bertha Winbush explained Council previously capped ARPA proposals at 70% up to $1 million, redirecting remaining funds to joint affordable housing projects, and committed to a February/March ARPA spend-down update.

agenda_items.title: ARPA Interlocal Agreement with Durham County for Joint Affordable Housing Projects
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Nate Baker pulled Item 7 to ask which projects would receive the $3.5 million county transfer (matched by $3.5 million from the city, bringing total joint ARPA housing funds to $27 million) and why eligibility was set up to 80% AMI. Community Development Director Reginald Johnson listed Cook Road repairs, Harriet's Place, Southside Phases 3 & 4, and Sandy Ridge, noting RFP rules require units at 30% and 60% AMI and below.

agenda_items.title: ShotSpotter / SoundThinking Three-Month Contract Extension Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Residents Asil (supporting ShotSpotter for shell-casing evidence near NCCU) and Manju Rajendran of Durham Beyond Policing (opposing the $52,356 extension) addressed the pilot. Police staff confirmed the Wilson Center study only evaluates the 12-month pilot data ending December 14, prompting Carl Rist and Javiera Caballero to question extending the contract while Mark-Anthony Middleton defended ShotSpotter's speed and effectiveness; Caballero moved the item to the General Business Agenda.

agenda_items.title: FY 2023 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR) Audit Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: External auditor Cherry Bekaert presented the FY23 audit dated November 15, issuing four unmodified (clean) opinions including a clean single audit of the Federal Transit Cluster and Powell Bill funds. Auditors reported zero material weaknesses and one significant deficiency regarding year-end accounts payable cutoff, which Finance Director Tim Flora and staff committed to addressing.

agenda_items.title: Ward 3 City Council Vacancy Process and Schedule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Procedures Chair Javiera Caballero and Deputy City Attorney Don O'Toole outlined choosing between City Charter Section 13.2 (60-day clock ending February 2, 2024 with a special-election fallback if deadlocked) or state statute. Council agreed by consensus to follow the 60-day Charter process, notice applications through December 21, finalize a questionnaire on December 19 (due January 3), hold interviews January 8, host supporter remarks January 10, and vote January 16.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Consensus on Charter process and timeline

agenda_items.title: Board Nominations and Settling of December 18 Regular Meeting Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk reported council nominations of Orlando Watson to the Durham Open Space and Trails Commission and Vanessa W. Smart to the Durham Cultural Advisory Board. City Manager Wanda Page read the December 18 agenda placement—Consent Items 1-10 and 12-16, GBA Item 11, and Public Hearings Items 17-22—which Council approved unanimously.

votes.item_title: Approve City Manager Priority Items (Item 4 ACFR Presentation & Item 19 Omnibus 18 Revision)
votes.discussion_detail: Council approved adding the City Manager's two priority items—a 20-minute presentation on the FY23 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (Item 4) and revised memo/attachments removing zero-lot-line house language from UDO Omnibus 18 (Item 19)—by hand vote.

votes.item_title: Set the Agenda for December 18, 2023 City Council Meeting (Consent: 1-10, 12-16; GBA: 11; Public Hearings: 17-22)
votes.discussion_detail: Council moved, seconded, and unanimously approved the December 18 regular meeting docket with Item 11 (ShotSpotter contract extension) moved to the General Business Agenda at Javiera Caballero's request.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Work Session Dec. 7, 2023
disagreements.issue: Extending ShotSpotter Pilot Contract for Three Months Pending Wilson Center Evaluation
disagreements.summary: Council members debated whether to keep ShotSpotter running for three months ($52,356) while the Wilson Center analyzes data from the already-concluding one-year pilot.
disagreements.side_a_position: Question extending the contract when no additional evaluation data will be collected and move the decision to the General Business Agenda for full public debate.
side_a_arguments: The Wilson Center evaluation is limited strictly to the 12-month pilot period ending December 14, so a 3-month extension yields no extra study data.
Extending an expired pilot without completed evaluation findings creates a slippery slope.
Public and council views warrant placing Item 11 on the General Business Agenda rather than Consent.
disagreements.side_b_position: Maintain continuity of ShotSpotter operations for three months rather than shutting sensors off mid-review.
side_b_arguments: ShotSpotter alerts have faster response times than 911 calls, led to arrests and gun recoveries, and alerted police when residents did not call 911.
No reports of aggressive policing from the pilot have materialized.
Deactivating sensors on December 14 while awaiting the report disrupts emergency response.
disagreements.resolution: Item 11 was pulled from Consent and placed on the December 18 General Business Agenda for a formal vote.

meetings.title: Durham City Council December 4, 2023
meetings.executive_summary: The December 4, 2023 organizational and regular City Council meeting opened with outgoing Mayor Elaine O'Neal presiding over the certification of the November 7, 2023 municipal election results and the swearing-in of Mayor Leonardo Williams alongside council members Carl Rist, Nate Baker, and Javiera Caballero. Upon assuming the gavel, Mayor Williams nominated Mark-Anthony Middleton as Mayor Pro Tempore (approved 5-1), and Council approved the Consent Agenda (6-0) while re-advertising Item 1 (Participatory Budgeting Steering Committee). In public hearings, Council continued the 5802 South Miami Boulevard annexation to January 2, unanimously approved rezoning the historic Greystone mansion at 618 Morehead Avenue (6-0), passed the eight-townhome Oaks at Gray rezoning on a 4-2 split (Nate Baker and DeDreana Freeman opposed), and unanimously accepted Leonardo Williams's resignation from the Ward 3 seat.

agenda_items.title: Election Certification, Swearing-In of New Council, and Selection of Mayor Pro Tempore
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Outgoing Mayor Elaine O'Neal opened the organizational meeting, received certified November 7, 2023 election results from Durham County Board of Elections Chair Dawn Baxton and Director Derek Bowens, and oversaw oaths of office for Leonardo Williams as Mayor and Nate Baker, Carl Rist, and Javiera Caballero as At-Large Council Members. After taking the gavel, Mayor Williams outlined policy coordination with Caballero and project leadership under Mark-Anthony Middleton, who was elected Mayor Pro Tempore 5-1.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Items 2-5, 7-21 (Item 1 Referred Back)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Williams read the consent agenda, noting Item 1 (Participatory Budgeting Steering Committee appointment) was referred back to staff to be re-advertised. Council approved Items 2 through 5 and 7 through 21—including the October sidewalk audit, utility revenue bond anticipation note, WD Hill playground contract, Q3 crime report, and NCDOT Hillandale Road agreement—by a 6-0 vote.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation: 5802 South Miami Boulevard Multi-Family
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a 540-unit multi-family annexation and rezoning request on 11 acres along South Miami Boulevard, and DeDreana Freeman asked staff to daylight census block demographic data in future reports. Applicant representative Marie Farmer of Parker Poe requested a continuance to January 2, 2024 to ensure compliance with updated phasing, grading, and tree coverage UDO standards, which Council granted by consensus.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: 618 Morehead Avenue (Greystone Mansion)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dan Jewell of Thomas & Hutton presented Hem + Spire's request to rezone the three-acre historic Greystone property at 618 Morehead Avenue from Office & Institutional to Commercial General with a graphic development plan to restore and preserve the vacant mansion. Morehead Hill residents Bruce Mitchell and David Ball strongly praised the developer's two-year neighborhood engagement, and Council unanimously approved both the rezoning and consistency statement 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: Oaks at Gray (321, 323, and 325 Gray Avenue)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Marie Farmer presented an RU-M textual development plan to allow up to eight 1,600-1,800 sq ft market-rate townhomes ($500k-$600k range) replacing two single-family homes, while neighbor Mr. Greener opposed added density beyond the five units allowed by right. Nate Baker questioned granting density without using affordable housing density bonuses and DeDreana Freeman sought design commitments and preservation of five-unit scale; the rezoning passed 4-2 and consistency passed 5-1.

agenda_items.title: Acceptance of Leonardo Williams's Ward 3 Seat Resignation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At the close of the meeting, Carl Rist moved to formally accept Leonardo Williams's resignation from the Ward 3 City Council seat upon his inauguration as Mayor. Council unanimously accepted the resignation before adjourning at 9:23 PM.

votes.item_title: Select Mark-Anthony Middleton as Mayor Pro Tempore
votes.notes: Mayor Williams initially misspoke '6-1' before correcting the record to '5-1'; the transcript did not verbally identify the single dissenting member.
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Leonardo Williams entertained a motion to select Mark-Anthony Middleton as Mayor Pro Tempore, explaining he would rely on Middleton for budget/project initiatives and Javiera Caballero for policy leadership. Following a motion and second, the hand vote passed 5-1.

votes.item_title: Item 24: Continue Consolidated Annexation 5802 South Miami Boulevard Multi-Family to January 2, 2024
votes.notes: Public hearing remained open until January 2, 2024.
votes.discussion_detail: At the applicant's request to evaluate compliance with new UDO phasing, grading, and tree-coverage standards, Council agreed by unanimous consent to continue the public hearing on 5802 South Miami Boulevard to January 2, 2024.

votes.item_title: Item 25 (Motion 1): Adopt UDO Zoning Map Amendment for 618 Morehead Avenue (OI(D) to CG(D))
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously approved rezoning 618 Morehead Avenue from Office & Institutional with a development plan to Commercial General with a graphic development plan in the Morehead Hill Local Historic District, preserving the historic Greystone mansion.

votes.item_title: Item 25 (Motion 2): Adopt NCGS 160D-605 Consistency Statement for 618 Morehead Avenue
votes.discussion_detail: Council unanimously adopted the statutory consistency statement for the 618 Morehead Avenue rezoning.

votes.item_title: Item 26 (Motion 1): Adopt UDO Zoning Map Amendment for Oaks at Gray (321, 323, 325 Gray Ave)
votes.discussion_detail: Council voted 4-2 to rezone three parcels at 321-325 Gray Avenue from RU-M to RU-M with a textual development plan permitting up to eight townhouses, over objections from Nate Baker and DeDreana Freeman regarding density bonuses, displacement, and neighborhood design fit.

votes.item_title: Item 26 (Motion 2): Adopt NCGS 160D-605 Consistency Statement for Oaks at Gray
votes.discussion_detail: Moved by Javiera Caballero and seconded by Carl Rist, Council adopted the consistency statement for Oaks at Gray 5-1, with Nate Baker voting no.

votes.item_title: Accept Resignation of Leonardo Williams from Ward 3 City Council Seat
votes.discussion_detail: Moved by Carl Rist and properly seconded, Council unanimously accepted Mayor Leonardo Williams's formal resignation from his Ward 3 City Council seat.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council December 4, 2023
disagreements.issue: Oaks at Gray Townhome Rezoning Density Bonus and Neighborhood Compatibility (321-325 Gray Ave)
disagreements.summary: Council split 4-2 over whether to rezone 0.435 acres in a predominantly single-family gentrifying neighborhood to allow eight market-rate townhouses instead of the five permitted by right.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the eight-townhouse rezoning as smaller, more attainable infill housing with off-street garage parking.
side_a_arguments: Building eight smaller 1,600-1,800 sq ft units yields lower price points than five larger townhomes allowed by right.
The project provides infill housing near downtown with garages and a small parking lot to address street parking concerns.
Local resident developers are investing in their first triangle project.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose granting three extra units by rezoning without using affordable housing density bonuses or single-family design commitments.
side_b_arguments: Granting extra units via rezoning undermines incentives for developers to use affordable housing density bonuses.
The property lies in a gentrifying neighborhood where $500k-$600k townhomes do not serve existing residents and exacerbate displacement.
The textual plan lacked design commitments to fit a predominantly single-family street and departed from the Established Residential place type.
disagreements.resolution: The zoning map change passed 4-2, and the consistency statement passed 5-1 (Nate Baker opposed).
